cancer_indication: Investigational PD-1 blockade in human breast cancer, with emerging use in PD-L1–positive triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and selected biomarker-enriched subgroups (e.g. BRCA1/2-mutated or HRD-positive tumors) based on class-effect data and early dostarlimab combination trials.
moa: Dostarlimab binds the PD-1 (PDCD1) receptor on activated T cells and blocks its interaction with PD-L1 and PD-L2, releasing PD-1–mediated co-inhibition and restoring T-cell proliferation, cytokine production and cytotoxic function against tumor cells in breast cancer. Its efficacy depends on an immune-inflamed tumor microenvironment with intact antigen presentation, T-cell receptor signaling and interferon responses, which is most commonly seen in PD-L1–positive TNBC, HER2-enriched and some BRCA1/2-mutated or HRD-positive tumors. Resistance arises when tumors downregulate antigen presentation or interferon signaling, or upregulate immunosuppressive pathways such as TGF-β, WNT/β-catenin, PI3K/AKT, IDO1/kynurenine and alternate checkpoint receptors.

REACTOME_CO_INHIBITION_BY_PD_1.description: PD-1 co-inhibitory immune checkpoint signaling in activated T cells, where engagement of PD-1 (PDCD1) by PD-L1/PD-L2 dampens T-cell receptor signaling, proliferation and cytokine production, limiting effector T-cell responses.
REACTOME_CO_INHIBITION_BY_PD_1.interpretation: In breast cancer, this pathway is the primary target of dostarlimab; blocking PD-1 co-inhibition reinvigorates tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and restores anti-tumor immunity, particularly in immune-inflamed TNBC and HER2-enriched tumors with pre-existing T-cell activity.

KEGG_T_CELL_RECEPTOR_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: T-cell receptor (TCR) signaling cascade triggered by recognition of peptide–MHC complexes, leading to activation of downstream kinases, transcription factors and effector functions in T cells.
KEGG_T_CELL_RECEPTOR_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation: Breast tumors with intact antigen presentation and robust TCR signaling (high MHC I, adequate costimulation and TILs) show better responses to PD-1 blockade with dostarlimab, whereas defects in antigen presentation or costimulation can render tumors resistant despite PD-1 inhibition.

HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE.description: Genes induced by interferon-gamma, reflecting a Th1-type inflammatory response including chemokines (e.g. CXCL9, CXCL10), antigen presentation molecules and immune activation markers.
HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE.interpretation: A high IFN-γ response signature in breast tumors, especially TNBC, correlates with a T-cell–inflamed microenvironment and predicts increased sensitivity to PD-1 inhibitors such as dostarlimab, while loss of IFN-γ responsiveness via JAK/STAT defects confers resistance.

KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_CGAS_STING_SIGNAL.description: Cytosolic DNA-sensing pathway centered on cGAS–STING, which detects double-stranded DNA in the cytosol and induces type I interferon and inflammatory cytokine production.
KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_CGAS_STING_SIGNAL.interpretation: In BRCA1/2-mutated and HRD-positive breast cancers, DNA damage activates cGAS–STING, promoting type I IFN signaling, dendritic cell activation and T-cell recruitment, thereby sensitizing tumors to dostarlimab, particularly in combinations with PARP inhibitors that further enhance STING activation.

GOBP_ANTIGEN_PROCESSING_AND_PRESENTATION.description: Processing of intracellular proteins into peptides and their loading onto MHC class I molecules for presentation to CD8+ T cells, involving components such as the immunoproteasome, TAP complex, tapasin, β2-microglobulin and HLA class I.
GOBP_ANTIGEN_PROCESSING_AND_PRESENTATION.interpretation: Breast tumors that maintain or upregulate MHC I antigen presentation are more susceptible to T-cell–mediated killing unleashed by dostarlimab, whereas loss of B2M, HLA class I or other antigen-processing components results in immune escape and resistance to PD-1 blockade.

HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING.description: Transforming growth factor-beta signaling through SMAD and non-SMAD pathways, regulating fibrosis, epithelial–mesenchymal transition, immune suppression and stromal remodeling.
HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING.interpretation: High TGF-β signaling in breast tumors and their stroma promotes immune exclusion, Treg and MDSC recruitment and IDO1 induction, and is associated with poor response or resistance to PD-1 inhibitors like dostarlimab, whereas suppression of TGF-β signaling can improve T-cell infiltration and sensitivity.

HALLMARK_WNT_BETA_CATENIN_SIGNALING.description: Canonical WNT signaling via β-catenin stabilization and nuclear translocation, controlling developmental programs, stemness and cell fate.
HALLMARK_WNT_BETA_CATENIN_SIGNALING.interpretation: Upregulated WNT/β-catenin signaling in basal-like and other breast cancers excludes dendritic cells and T cells from the tumor microenvironment, creating immune-cold tumors that resist dostarlimab, while downregulation of this pathway is linked to improved TIL priming and checkpoint inhibitor responsiveness.

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: PI3K–AKT–mTOR intracellular signaling axis driving cell growth, survival, metabolism and proliferation downstream of growth factor and oncogenic inputs.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: Hyperactive PI3K–AKT signaling (e.g. via PTEN loss) in breast tumors promotes an immunosuppressive milieu with reduced antigen presentation and TILs and increased VEGF and other factors, contributing to resistance to dostarlimab, whereas pharmacologic or genetic attenuation of this pathway can enhance immune infiltration and PD-1 blockade efficacy.

GOBP_TOLERANCE_INDUCTION_DEPENDENT_UPON_.description: Immune processes that induce peripheral tolerance following immune activation, including the induction of regulatory T cells and production of suppressive mediators such as IDO1, TGF-β and IL-10.
GOBP_TOLERANCE_INDUCTION_DEPENDENT_UPON_.interpretation: In breast cancer, chronic immune activation and PD-1 pathway engagement can drive tolerance programs (e.g. Treg accumulation, IDO1 and IL-10 upregulation), establishing an immunosuppressive microenvironment that counteracts the reinvigorated T cells produced by dostarlimab.

GOBP_L_TRYPTOPHAN_CATABOLIC_PROCESS_TO_K.description: Catabolism of L-tryptophan to kynurenine, largely mediated by indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1), generating metabolites that modulate immune responses.
GOBP_L_TRYPTOPHAN_CATABOLIC_PROCESS_TO_K.interpretation: High IDO1-driven tryptophan catabolism in breast tumors depletes tryptophan and accumulates immunosuppressive kynurenines, promoting T-cell dysfunction and regulatory T-cell expansion, thereby conferring resistance to dostarlimab; conversely, low IDO1 activity or pathway inhibition is associated with improved checkpoint inhibitor responses.

REACTOME_INTERLEUKIN_10_SIGNALING.description: Interleukin-10 signaling pathway, in which IL-10 engages its receptor to activate downstream JAK–STAT signaling and exert anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects.
REACTOME_INTERLEUKIN_10_SIGNALING.interpretation: Elevated IL-10 signaling in the breast tumor microenvironment contributes to a 'cold' immunosuppressive state with limited T-cell activation, and is described as part of cytokine milieus that blunt the effectiveness of PD-1 blockade with dostarlimab.

KEGG_JAK_STAT_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: Janus kinase (JAK)–signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) cascades downstream of cytokine receptors (including IFN and IL-6 family receptors), governing transcriptional responses to cytokines.
KEGG_JAK_STAT_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation: Intact JAK–STAT signaling is required for breast cancer cells to respond to IFN-γ by upregulating MHC I and pro-apoptotic programs under PD-1 blockade; loss-of-function mutations in JAK1/2 or downregulation of IFNGR/IRF1 abrogate these responses and are implicated as mechanisms of resistance to dostarlimab, while chronic IL-6/STAT3 activation supports immunosuppressive MDSCs and macrophages that also limit benefit.

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: High baseline CXCL9 expression is part of an IFN-γ–related, T-cell–inflamed gene expression profile in breast cancer that correlates with greater sensitivity to PD-1 blockade, reflecting enhanced recruitment and activation of CXCR3+ effector T cells.

CXCL10 is another IFN-γ–inducible chemokine whose elevated expression marks an immune-inflamed TNBC microenvironment with abundant TILs, and increased CXCL10 is associated with improved responses to PD-1 inhibitors such as dostarlimab.

Upregulation of STING1 (STING pathway) and related genes in HRD-positive and BRCA-mutated breast tumors promotes type I interferon production and dendritic cell activation, enhancing CD8+ T-cell priming and sensitizing these tumors to dostarlimab, particularly in PARP inhibitor combinations.

Increased IFNB1 expression reflects active cGAS–STING signaling and type I interferon responses in breast cancers that respond to PD-1 blockade, supporting enhanced immune recognition and improved benefit from dostarlimab.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Breast tumors with low baseline IDO1 expression or limited induction of the IDO1–kynurenine pathway exhibit less tryptophan depletion and immunosuppressive metabolite production, which is associated with better T-cell function and improved responses to PD-1 inhibitors including dostarlimab.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: High IDO1 expression in breast tumors drives tryptophan catabolism to kynurenine, suppressing effector T cells and promoting regulatory T cells; in TNBC and other settings, high baseline IDO1 has been associated with worse outcomes on immune checkpoint inhibitors, indicating resistance to PD-1 blockade.

HAVCR2 (TIM-3) is upregulated on tumor-infiltrating T cells after PD-1 blockade as an adaptive resistance mechanism; increased TIM-3 expression in post-therapy breast cancer samples signifies continued T-cell exhaustion and reduced efficacy of dostarlimab.

LAG3 is another inhibitory checkpoint receptor that is upregulated on TILs in breast tumors that do not respond to PD-1 therapy, contributing to redundant inhibitory signaling that limits the benefit of dostarlimab.

Increased infiltration of FOXP3+ regulatory T cells has been observed in breast tumors progressing on PD-1 inhibitors, reflecting expansion of immunosuppressive Tregs that counteract the reinvigorated effector T cells induced by dostarlimab.

CCL22 expression recruits CCR4+ regulatory T cells into the breast tumor microenvironment; upregulation of CCL22 in tumors progressing on PD-1 therapy is implicated in Treg-mediated resistance to dostarlimab.

CCR4 on regulatory T cells mediates their chemotaxis in response to ligands such as CCL22; high CCR4-dependent Treg trafficking supports an immunosuppressive niche that undermines the anti-tumor activity of dostarlimab.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss-of-function mutations or downregulation of B2M in breast tumors result in loss of MHC class I surface expression, preventing CD8+ T cells from recognizing tumor antigens and causing resistance to PD-1 blockade with dostarlimab.

Reduced HLA-A expression and broader HLA class I downregulation have been observed in metastatic breast cancer lesions that fail PD-1 therapy, indicating that diminished MHC I presentation contributes to escape from dostarlimab-induced T-cell killing.

Inactivating mutations in JAK1 abrogate interferon signaling in tumor cells so that IFN-γ released by T cells cannot induce MHC I or growth arrest, a mechanism described in PD-1–refractory cancers and implicated in resistance to dostarlimab.

JAK2 loss-of-function mutations have been reported in metastatic TNBC resistant to pembrolizumab, and by analogy such defects prevent IFN-γ–driven upregulation of antigen presentation and apoptosis, conferring resistance to PD-1 blockade including dostarlimab.

Downregulation of IFNGR1 reduces tumor cell responsiveness to IFN-γ, limiting induction of PD-L1, MHC I and pro-apoptotic genes, and is described as one way tumors escape the immune pressure unleashed by PD-1 inhibitors.

Reduced IFNGR2 expression similarly impairs IFN-γ receptor signaling in breast cancer cells, preventing full execution of interferon-mediated anti-tumor programs despite active T cells under dostarlimab therapy.

Loss or downregulation of IRF1, a key transcription factor for IFN-γ responses, blunts induction of PD-L1, CXCL9 and other immunogenic genes in tumor cells, contributing to resistance to PD-1 blockade in breast cancer.

Downregulation or loss of the death receptor FAS on breast cancer cells diminishes their susceptibility to Fas/FasL-mediated apoptosis by cytotoxic T cells, enabling survival despite dostarlimab-mediated T-cell activation.

Low expression of the costimulatory ligand CD80 on antigen-presenting cells in the breast tumor microenvironment impairs T-cell priming and costimulation, which can lead to primary resistance where PD-1 blockade alone cannot fully activate T cells.

Reduced CD86 levels on dendritic cells and other APCs weaken CD28-mediated costimulatory signaling to T cells, contributing to ineffective T-cell activation and resistance to dostarlimab even when PD-1 is blocked.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC): TNBC is the subtype with the most immunotherapy data. It’s typically high in PD-L1 expression and TILs. Clinical trials (e.g. KEYNOTE-355, IMpassion130) showed that adding PD-1/L1 inhibitors to chemotherapy improves outcomes primarily in PD-L1–positive TNBC . Dostarlimab is not yet standard in TNBC, but as a PD-1 class drug it’s expected to behave like pembrolizumab. Evidence: a meta-analysis of PD-(L)1 trials in advanced TNBC confirmed improved survival, especially in PD-L1^+ patients . In early TNBC, neoadjuvant PD-1 inhibition plus chemo significantly raises pCR rates (e.g. ~60% vs 40% in KEYNOTE-522). Biomarker analyses show that basal-like TNBC responds better than mesenchymal subtypes, and high TIL counts predict benefit. On the other hand, TNBC tumors with high TGF-β or lacking immune infiltration derive minimal benefit . Ongoing trials (IMpassion132, KEYNOTE-552) and real-world studies are evaluating dostarlimab in TNBC, particularly in those who progress on first-line pembrolizumab or in PD-L1^ cases combined with other immunomodulators.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR+/HER2– (Luminal A & B): These estrogen receptor–positive tumors are generally “colder” immunologically. Single-agent checkpoint inhibitors have low response rates (<10%) in metastatic HR+ breast cancer. However, select subgroups show promise: e.g., HR+ tumors with gBRCA1/2 mutations or high TMB might respond due to higher neoantigen loads. A recent Phase II trial (TBCRC 056 arm C) in ER+/HER2–, BRCA-mutated patients gave neoadjuvant niraparib + dostarlimab; it achieved a 17% pCR rate and 44% near-pCR – notable for this subtype. This suggests immunotherapy can work in luminal cancers if DNA repair is compromised (HRD) and an immune response can be stimulated . Additionally, an exploratory study reported that adding pembrolizumab to chemo in early high-risk Luminal B cancers significantly improved pCR from ~13% to 27% , indicating some chemo-immune synergy even in ER+ disease. Biomarker insights: luminal tumors with high immune gene expression (an “immune hot” subset ~5–10% of cases) had better than expected responses to ICIs in trials. Conversely, most luminal cancers have active estrogen signaling which can suppress immune responses (e.g. via IL-6/STAT3); ongoing studies are examining if therapies like CDK4/6 inhibitors (which have immunomodulatory effects) combined with PD-1 blockade can enhance efficacy in ER+ disease.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-Positive: HER2^+ breast cancers are moderately immunogenic; they often have substantial TILs, and some anti-HER2 therapies can induce immune responses (ADCC). Combining PD-1 inhibitors with HER2-targeted therapy is a logical strategy. The Phase III KEYNOTE-811 trial in HER2+ gastric cancer (trastuzumab + chemo ± pembrolizumab) showed improved response rates , which has influenced breast cancer research. In breast cancer, early-phase data: in the PANACEA study (phase Ib/II), pembrolizumab plus trastuzumab had a 15% response rate in PD-L1^+ metastatic HER2+ patients who had progressed on trastuzumab . Another trial (KATE2) combining atezolizumab with T-DM1 in advanced HER2+ was negative overall, but hinted that PD-L1^+ patients might benefit. Neoadjuvant trials are ongoing: e.g., I-SPY2 showed that adding pembrolizumab to chemo + HER2-targeted therapy improved pCR in HER2+ (especially in hormone receptor–negative, HER2+ cases). Biomarker notes: HER2-enriched intrinsic subtype (which is often ER–/HER2+) has high immune activation and may derive the most benefit, whereas luminal HER2+ (ER+/HER2+) tumors are less immune-infiltrated. Also, PI3K pathway mutations (common in HER2+ disease) might limit immunotherapy efficacy by immune-evasion mechanisms , so combinations with PI3K inhibitors are of interest.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.BRCA1/2-Mutated and HRD-Positive: This spans across subtypes (many BRCA1 are TNBC, BRCA2 often luminal B). BRCA-mutant breast cancers have DNA repair defects leading to genomic instability and potential immune visibility. They also accumulate lymphocytes; for instance, BRCA1 associated TNBCs usually have higher TILs than sporadic TNBCs. Clinical evidence: the aforementioned neoadjuvant PARP + dostarlimab trial in BRCA-mutant ER+ patients showed immunotherapy activity in a setting where normally it would be minimal . Another example: a small cohort of metastatic BRCA1/2-mutant breast cancer patients had improved disease control with checkpoint inhibitors in some reports (e.g., case series using pembrolizumab post-platinum). It’s hypothesized that HRD tumors may respond better due to more neoantigens and cGAS–STING activation from DNA damage . However, not all HRD tumors respond – some BRCA2 luminal tumors remain immune-cold. Ongoing trials like KEYNOTE-BRCA (PD-1 ± PARP inhibitor in BRCA mutated metastatic BC) will shed light. Additionally, PALB2-mutated breast cancers (which are HRD) were included with BRCA in TBCRC 056 and showed similar immune changes .
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Basal-like vs. Other TNBC Subtypes: Within TNBC, intrinsic subtypes matter. Basal-like TNBC (which overlaps with immunomodulatory subtype) tends to respond to ICIs if PD-L1^+. In contrast, mesenchymal and luminal-androgen receptor (LAR) subtypes of TNBC have lower response rates. Basal-like tumors often have high TILs and PD-L1; in the IMpassion130 trial, patients with basal-like signatures had the largest benefit from atezolizumab. PD-L1 expression is highest in the basal-like/ immune-activated subgroup. LAR TNBCs (which express AR) are usually cold; interestingly, a clinical trial of AR inhibitor + pembrolizumab is exploring if turning off AR can inflame these tumors. Claudin-low breast cancers (which are often TNBC or metaplastic) have high immune infiltration but also high immunosuppressive features (Tregs, checkpoint expression); some have responded to ICIs, but others progress rapidly (likely due to macrophage/TGF-β–rich milieu). For metaplastic TNBC, small studies reported relatively high response rates (~20–30%) to PD-1 inhibitors, suggesting this rare subtype (often PD-L1^+) may be sensitive.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Luminal A vs. Luminal B: Among HR+ cancers, Luminal B (high Ki-67, more HER2-enriched gene expression) has slightly more immune infiltration than Luminal A. It’s hypothesized that Luminal B might gain a bit more from immunotherapy, especially in the high-proliferation, endocrine-resistant setting. The I-SPY2 trial arm with pembrolizumab did show some pCR improvements in ER+ (most of whom were Luminal B) . Luminal A, being lower grade and low proliferation, rarely has substantial TILs and has shown almost no ICI activity in metastatic trials. In early-stage, if Luminal A tumors are low-risk, immunotherapy is not being considered. In metastatic luminal disease, combinations like pembrolizumab with endocrine therapy did not show clear benefit (KEYPNOTE-028 and JAVELIN trials had minimal responses in ER+ cohorts). Research is ongoing into whether induced hypermutation (e.g. using APOBEC induction or CDK4/6 inhibitor’s immunomodulatory effect) could render Luminal A tumors more immunogenic.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-Enriched vs. Other HER2+: “HER2-enriched” is an intrinsic subtype (by gene expression) found in some HER2+ tumors (and some HER2-). HER2-enriched tumors have higher immune signatures on average than the Luminal HER2 subtype. Post-hoc analyses from the KATE2 trial hinted that patients with HER2-enriched profiles had numerically better outcomes with atezolizumab + T-DM1 compared to T-DM1 alone, whereas those with luminal profiles did not – aligning with the idea that the HER2 enriched subtype (often non-luminal) is more immunotherapy-responsive. Additionally, ERBB2 driven oncogenic pathways can induce PI3K/AKT; patients whose HER2+ tumors also carry PIK3CA mutations might respond less to immunotherapy due to PI3K-mediated immunosuppression . There’s interest in combining PI3Kα inhibitors with ICIs in this subset.
